subject: SIG: KEK lifecycle & HSM rotation — evidence and plan
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice@fintech-co.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: encryption section — KMS/HSM rotation questions

Diego,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the SIG questionnaire. Our security team had a focused pass on the encryption section and flagged a few follow-ups specifically around key lifecycle and HSM integration. We need short, evidence-backed answers for the following items for our SOC2 review:

1) Do you use an HSM for root/KEK storage or do you rely on cloud-managed KMS only? Please specify vendor(s) and deployment mode (managed service vs customer-provided).
2) What is your KEK rotation schedule and who (roles) has the ability to trigger rotation?
3) Describe envelope encryption flow (DEK/KEK) and whether customers can BYOK/CMK.
4) Auditability: can you provide a sample audit trail showing KMS rotation events and admin actions (redacted)?
5) Key backup/escrow: how are long-term backups protected and who controls them?

Can you return answers and any supporting artifacts (diagrams, playbooks, logs) by EOD Monday? If helpful, we can book a short demo.

Appreciate it,
Alice
Security Operations
FinTech Co

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@fintech-co.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: encryption section — KMS/HSM rotation questions

Alice — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a short one-page summary (redwood_kms_summary.pdf). I’ll follow up with a more detailed playbook and a sample audit extract.

1) HSM usage: We protect KEKs in FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSMs. For the Redwood hosted offering we use AWS CloudHSM (customer-configured clusters in dedicated VPCs) and Thales Luna for select Dedicated/Private deployments. Root KEKs are generated and wrapped inside the HSM; we do not export raw root material.

2) Rotation schedule & triggers: KEKs (key-encryption keys) are rotated on a 12-month calendar cycle by default; a rolling 90-day policy is available for higher-risk customers. Rotations can be initiated by the Security Engineering team or by an automated policy orchestrator; only principals in the "KeyOps" role (separate from infra admins) can approve manual rotations. We’ll include the role ARNs in the playbook.

3) Envelope flow / BYOK: We use envelope encryption — DEKs are generated per-model or per-session and encrypted with KEKs held in the HSM/KMS. Customers can use CMKs via BYOK for Dedicated/Private (customer-import or external KMS integration). For hosted customers we support SSE-KMS with customer-managed keys (CMKs) via Bring-Your-Own-Key integrations (subject to contractual controls).

4) Auditability: KMS events emit to our immutable audit pipeline (write-once S3 + append-only event stream) with event signatures. I’ve attached a sanitized sample of rotation events (audit-log-sample.txt).

5) Backup/escrow: Long-term backup of wrapped KEKs is stored in an encrypted vault (HSM-wrapped and double-wrapped with a secondary escrow key). Access to escrow requires multi-party approval (3-of-5) via the hardware-backed approval appliance.

Next steps: I’ll circulate the rotation playbook (detailed steps, runbooks, screenshots) and can schedule a 30-min demo of a rotation in our test environment this week. CC’ing Kim and Neha for any technical details I missed.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-23T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: encryption section — KMS/HSM rotation questions

Diego — quick clarifications to add to the playbook before we send the consolidated packet to FinTech Co:

- Rotation details: automated rotations create a new KEK inside the HSM, re-wrap all active DEKs using an online rewrap (non-blocking) and mark old KEKs as deprecated for 30 days before scheduled destruction. We keep a 90-day grace window to support rollback/forensics.
- Key custodians: list out the KeyOps principals (we should not include personal emails in the pack; reference roles instead).
- HSM vendor specifics: for CloudHSM we include cluster ARNs and KMS key aliases; for Thales we include firmware version and module cert references (not the serials).

I’ve added these bullets into the draft playbook. Vivek — can you confirm the multi-party escrow appliance name and MFA gating step?

-Neha

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@fintech-co.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-24T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SIG: KEK lifecycle & HSM rotation — evidence and plan

Alice — forwarding an updated playbook (kms_rotation_playbook_v2.docx) with the extra clarifications Neha suggested plus a redacted sample audit extract attached. Highlights included in the playbook: rotation runbook (pre-checks, re-wrap steps, post-checks), role separation matrix, HSM vendor modes, and emergency rotation procedure.

Quick summary of the rotation runbook steps (from playbook):
- Stage: create new KEK inside HSM, snapshot cluster state.
- Re-wrap: re-encrypt active DEKs with new KEK using online rewrap in batches (low-latency path retained).
- Validate: run integrity check across sample sessions, confirm token-level decryption success.
- Deprecate: mark old KEK as deprecated; maintain wrapped backups encrypted with escrow key.
- Destroy: after 30-day grace and compliance sign-off, schedule secure deletion in HSM per vendor delete flow.

Attachments: kms_rotation_playbook_v2.docx, audit-log-sample.txt

If you want we can do a live run with a test KEK in our sandbox — happy to set that up.

Best,
Diego

From: Alice Monroe <alice@fintech-co.com>

Diego / team — thanks, this looks good and addresses our immediate SIG follow-ups. A couple of follow-ups before we close the ticket:

- Please share a short redacted screenshot or screencast of the KMS rotation audit showing the admin action and event id (we need one visual artifact).
- Can you confirm whether the 12-month default rotation is applied per-customer or globally? Our compliance team wants per-tenant rotation option.

If you can drop the screenshot and a one-line confirmation on per-tenant option, we can mark the SIG encryption section as closed. Happy to take the demo next week if needed.

Thanks — Alice
